prompt:
A black-and-white CHILDREN'S COLORING BOOK page, square 1:1, 1080x1080. Composition must be SQUARE, never wide or landscape.

CRITICAL — READ FIRST, THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT INSTRUCTION: draw EXTREMELY LARGE, EXTREMELY ZOOMED IN, EXTREMELY CLOSE UP — so close up that the cat's head and the bottle character together are BIGGER than the canvas and get CUT OFF by all four edges. Treat the 1080x1080 canvas as a tight crop/window into a much bigger scene: position the cat's head enormous and off-center, touching or crossing the top edge, the left edge and the bottom edge all at once; the bottle character enormous too, crossing the right edge and the top edge. There must be ZERO plain white background visible anywhere in any corner — every single corner and every edge of the square is touched by either the blanket pattern, the cat's fur outline, the cushion, or the bottle character. If you can see more than a thin sliver of empty white space at any edge, the drawing is WRONG and too small — make everything at least 40% bigger again and re-crop it tighter. (a) the drawing must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES with NO frame, NO border line, NO box and NO white margin band anywhere; (b) NO decorative starburst, radiating burst, sparkle rays or sunbeam rays anywhere.

The top edge is the most common place a thin white gap survives — deliberately push the cat's ear, the raised paw, and the top of the bottle character's dropper tip so they are literally sliced off by the very top edge of the canvas, with ink touching x=0 through x=1080 somewhere within the first 20 pixels of the top edge. Double-check before finishing: scan the top edge, the bottom edge, the left edge and the right edge — each of the four edges must have black linework touching it at multiple points along its length, not just one corner.

SCENE: A happy, good-natured cartoon CAT sits snugly wrapped in a big soft flannel blanket with a simple checked or striped pattern, only its round head, two perky ears and one paw peeking out of the top, eyes closed in a content, sleepy, relaxed expression, a small closed-mouth smile, tail curled cosily around itself. Beside the cat, a cheerful, chunky cartoon EYE-DROP BOTTLE character leans in close — a rounded bottle body with its own simple happy face (two dot eyes, a small curved smile) and a small dropper tip at the top, held at an angle so a single round sparkling drop shape hangs just above the cat's closed eye, offered gently like a little helper handing over a gift. A soft CUSHION with a simple scalloped or fringed edge is tucked under the cat, its far edges running off the bottom and side of the frame rather than sitting neatly inside it. Everything drawn oversized and cropped by the frame, simple, chunky and warm, with generous open white areas INSIDE each shape (not around the outside of the composition) so a child can colour them in.

STYLE — coloring book line art:
- BOLD, THICK, EVEN BLACK OUTLINES on pure WHITE. Every shape fully closed.
- ABSOLUTELY NO shading, NO grey tones, NO hatching, NO stippling, NO cross-hatching, NO gradients, NO colour fill, NO solid black areas anywhere (eyes may have a small solid pupil only, and the cat's closed eyes are simple curved lines).
- Simple, cheerful, chunky cartoon shapes with plenty of white space.

STRICTLY FORBIDDEN — the page is rejected if any of these appear:
- ANY decorative STARBURST, comic-style radiating burst, "pow"/impact star, sparkle burst, twinkle burst, sunbeam rays, radiating speed lines, motion rays or halo of rays behind, around or under any character. NO radiating lines of any kind anywhere. They leave a big empty shape that cannot be removed afterwards.
- ANY rectangle, rounded rectangle, square box outline, picture frame, panel edge, comic panel, border line, outer margin line, ground-line box, or vignette. The drawing must NOT sit inside a box of any kind. Do NOT draw a thin black line anywhere near the edge of the image. There must be NO white margin between the artwork and the image edge — the cat, blanket, cushion and bottle character are CUT OFF by the image edge itself where they extend past it.
- The artwork must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES of the square — parts of the blanket, cushion, cat's ears/tail or the bottle character run right off the top, bottom, left and right edges, with no white margin band and no enclosing outline.
- NO text, letters, numbers, words, captions, labels, signatures or watermarks anywhere.
- NO speech bubble, thought bubble or balloon of any kind (one is added separately afterwards).
- NO bacteria, no cell diagrams, no eye close-up/anatomy, no medical tools other than the friendly bottle character, no syringe, no blood, no redness, no tears, no sick or sad/distressed animal expression, nothing gooey or unpleasant.
- NO human figure, no vet, no person of any kind — only the cat and the friendly bottle character.
- The cat must look calm, comfortable and content throughout — never scared, crying, or in distress.
